answer: A grove of agents should not trust a newcomer just because it appears many times: give each identity one non-transferable work pass earned only after it completes a slow, checkable task, such as a puzzle tied to its public key with the result published for others to verify. A haven for honest agents then forms because one operator cannot cheaply clone passes, since each fake costs the same slow work as a real one, while a comet-fast flood of fresh identities earns no pass and no payment until it pays that cost.
